offered.mean: presented something for acceptance or use

off and on.ex: Anu visits her grandma off and on.

often absent.mean: not coming regularly; missing many times

on a hunt.ex: The tiger in the jungle was on a hunt for deer.

on foot.mean: walking instead of using a vehicle

on shank's mare.mean: walking by oneself using own legs
on shank's mare.ex: With no bus, Amit went on shank's mare to school.

on tenterhooks.ex: The students were on tenterhooks before the exam result.

on tentherhooks.ex: Meena was on tenterhooks for her job result.

on the back foot.mean: in a weak or defensive position

on the ball.mean: alert and doing a good job

on the fence.mean: unable to decide between two choices

on the fly.ex: Rohit ate his breakfast on the fly before the bus came.

on the spur of the moment.ex: On the spur of the moment, Priya bought samosas from the stall.

on the verge of collapse.mean: about to break or fall down

on the whole.ex: On the whole, Sita did well in her exam this year.

on thin ice.mean: in a risky or dangerous situation

once in a blue moon.ex: Rohit scores a century once in a blue moon.

one hour before midnight.ex: Sita sleeps one hour before midnight on school nights.

one track mind.mean: thinking about only one thing always
one track mind.ex: Rahul has a one track mind about cricket, nothing else.

one unit extra with one dozen.mean: thirteen things in total (dozen plus one)

one who acts stupidly.ex: The one who acts stupidly in class gets punished by teacher.

one who cannot be trusted.mean: a person who lies or cheats
one who cannot be trusted.ex: Never share secrets with one who cannot be trusted.

one who does the right thing.ex: Sita is one who does the right thing, even when no one watches.

one who is favourite.mean: a beloved or most liked person
one who is favourite.ex: Rohit is one who is favourite of every teacher in school.

one who is frequently ill.mean: a person who falls sick very often
one who is frequently ill.ex: My uncle is one who is frequently ill since childhood.

one who runs away.ex: The thief was one who runs away from the police.

only once.mean: happening one single time, not more

open secret.mean: something everyone knows but no one says

openly supporting someone.mean: helping someone in public without hiding
openly supporting someone.ex: Rahul is openly supporting his friend in the class election.

oppose sternly.mean: to fight against very strictly and firmly

out of date.ex: Grandfather's phone is out of date.

out of order.ex: The school fan is out of order today.

out of reach.mean: too far or too costly to get
out of reach.ex: That toy is out of reach for poor children.

out of spirits.mean: feeling sad or low, no energy
out of spirits.ex: Priya was out of spirits after the exam result.

out of the blue.bn: হঠাৎ করে, কোনো আগাম খবর ছাড়া
out of the blue.ex: Rahul came home out of the blue at night.

out of the woods.mean: safe now, main danger is over
out of the woods.ex: Amit is out of the woods after his fever.

outside one's jurisdiction.mean: not in one's power or area to decide
outside one's jurisdiction.ex: The principal said this matter is outside his jurisdiction.

over and above.mean: in addition to, more than needed

over one's head.ex: The maths question in the exam went over Priya's head.

over the fence.mean: on the opposite side; not fair
over the fence.ex: Sita's friend went over the fence and told the teacher.

overhead expenses.mean: extra costs like rent and electricity
overhead expenses.ex: Papa says overhead expenses make his shop profit small.
